full_judgment:
4. Petitioner having not stated as to how and under what authority he was appointed Mutawalli we directed the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to produce the relevant file and the same was duly produced at the time of hearing of the Rule. Petitioner also filed as affidavit-in-reply. We have perused the file of HC No. 11278, petition, affidavit-in-opposition, affidavit-in-reply and other relevant papers and on consideration of the same along with order sheet of SC Case No. 11278 we find that the waqf in question was enrolled for the first time by order dated 29-11-47 and one Abdul Hafiz, son of Samiruddin, was appointed Mutawalli. Admittedly, there is no waqf deed and in the CS Khatian property of the said waqf was recorded as a Lakheraj waqf property under the Dhaka Nawab Court of Wards Estate showing Nawab Khwaja Salimullah as Mutawalli. It appears that Samiruddin, grandfather of the petitioner, was Khadem of the Mazar situated in the waqf property. Subsequently, in his order dated 28-8-48 Commissioner of Waqfs observed that as per CS Khatian Nawab Khwaja Salimullah was Mutawalli and father of Bashiruddin and Abdul Hafiz was the Khadem. Subsequently, by order dated 18-5-49 Commissioner of Waqfs declared Nawab Habibullah Bahadur as Mutwalli and vacated his earlier order dated 29-11-47 appointing Abdul Hafiz as the Mutwalli and by order dated 29-1-50 Nawab Bahadur was appointed Mutwalli. Subsequently by order dated 31-12-56 Bashiruddin was appointed as ad-interim Mutwalli under section 40 of the Bengal Waqfs Act, 1934 until further orders or till the order is set aside by a Court of competent jurisdiction. The said Mutwalli at the advanced state of his age on 4-12-79 filed an application for appointing his eldest son the petitioner as the mutwalli, Thereafter he having died on 17-12-79 his son present petitioner was substituted as mutwalli on 22-12-79. 

 "40 In the case of any waqfs of which there is no mutawalli or where there appears to the Board to be an impediment to the appointment of a mutwalli the Board, subject to any order of a competent Court, may appoint for such period as it thinks fit a person to act as mutwalli." 

 From the above it appears that the said provision has some similarity with the provision of section 43 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962. But there are some distinctions between the two provisions. Section 40 provides that appointment made under that section shall be subject to any order of the competent Court and the Commissioner of Waqfs may appoint a person as mutwalli for such period as it thinks fit. We have already noticed from order dated 31-12-56 that Bashiruddin Shah was appointed ad-interim mutwalli until further order or till the order is set aside by a Court of competent jurisdiction. Though the petitioner was substituted as mutwalli in place of his father Bashiruddin he cannot claim better status than that of his father and, as such, he is liable to be removed by the Administrator of Waqfs at any time. 

 6. It appears that respondent No. 4 filed an application to the Administrator of Waqfs proposing to construct a 16-storied building by the side of the PirYeameni Waqf Market in the remaining land and thereafter a meeting was held in the Ministry on 18-7-95 presided over by the Secretary and it was decided for development of the land near the PirYeameni Market. Thereafter by memo dated 25-11-97 Government appointed a Committee consisting of the Administrator of Waqfs as the convener, Deputy Secretary of the Ministry of Religious Affairs, the petitioner, a representative of the respondent No. 4 Prince Construction and the Deputy Administrator of Waqfs Dhaka as members for implementation of the scheme for the development of the land by the side of the Pir Yeameni Waqf Market. It appears from office note dated 26-10-97 that previously a committee was appointed for the construction of the PirYeameni Market with the Administrator of Waqfs as the Chairman and the petitioner gave his opinion for development of the entire land by his letter dated 25-6-90. By Memo dated 26-11-97 (Annexure-A) Administrator of Waqfs informed the petitioner and other members about the formation of the said committee. On 8-12-97 a meeting of the said committee was held attended by the petitioner and others and it was decided to consider the development proposal of different companies. On 19-1-98 another meeting of the said committee was held attended by the petitioner and others and in the said meeting two proposals for development of the said land was considered and proposal of respondent No. 4 was accepted. It was further decided on the proposal of the petitioner that foundation should be of a 20-storied building. It was further decided that advice of the local and foreign consultants are to be taken for implementation of the scheme vide Annexure-B. Another meeting of the said committee was held on 24-2-98 attended, amongst others by the petitioner's authorized representative and in that meeting it was decided that respondent No. 4 shall supply a draft copy of the agreement dated 11-2-98 to the petitioner and the petitioner would file a copy of the agreement by 5-3-98 and after receipt of his draft copy of the agreement the next meeting would be held for finalization of the agreement. Legal Adviser of the Waqf and Engineering Consultant were requested to give their opinion regarding the agreement for construction of the proposed building. Thereafter by letter dated 26-2-98 petitioner was directed to supply the copy of the draft agreement by 5-3-98. Another meeting of the said committee was held on 19-3-98 attended, amongst others, by the petitioner's representative and it was decided to allow the petitioner 6 days time to file the draft copy of the agreement and also decided to incorporate the opinion of the consultant dated 3-3- 98 in the draft copy of the agreement at the time of finalization of the same. By letter dated 25-3-98 (Annexure-D) petitioner's son Nasiruddin Shah informed the respondent No. 2 that his father had undergone heart operation and prayed for time. Thereafter by letter dated 30-3-98 respondent No. 3 on behalf of the respondent No. 2 asked Waqf Inspector to hold an enquiry to ascertain as to whether mutwalli was in a position to manage the waqf estate. Thereafter the said Inspector held an enquiry on 31-3-99 in presence of the petitioner, his son who filed the application on his behalf and 4 others and found the petitioner bed ridden with illness. He submitted his report on 1-4-98 vide Annexure- V. In the said report it was stated that development activities of the waqf was suspended due to the illness of the petitioner for a long time, and the petitioner would not be in a position to manage the waqf estate. Thereafter, by the impugned memo dated 6-4-98 respondent No.2 in the greater interest of the waqf estate and acceleration of the development scheme approved by the Ministry relieved the petitioner from the office of a mutwalli and Md. Abdul Jalil Bhuiyan Deputy Administrator of Waqfs (1) was appointed official mutwalli under section 44 of the said Ordinance until further orders. Being aggrieved by the same petitioner moved this Court and obtained this Rule and order of stay on 22-6-98.
